name: TS5A3160DCKR
title: 1 Ω SPDT analog switch, 1.65 V to 5.5 V
summary: A single-pole double-throw CMOS analog switch: COM connects to NC while the control input IN is low and to NO while it is high, closing the new path before opening the old one. It runs from one 1.65 V to 5.5 V supply and passes signals from 0 V to V+ in either direction with about 0.7 Ω ON resistance at 4.5 V. The control input takes up to 5.5 V at any supply, the switch terminals stay isolated with V+ = 0, and supply current is typically 5 nA to 10 nA. It comes in 6-pin SOT-23 (DBV) and SC70 (DCK), rated -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: 0.7 Ω typ, 0.9 Ω max at V+ = 4.5 V, 25 °C
make-before-break, tMBB 7 ns typ at 5 V
-64 dB at 10 MHz / -64 dB at 1 MHz
36.5 pC at 5 V, 5.5 pC at 1.8 V
10 nA typ, 50 nA max at 5.5 V, 25 °C

circuits.title: System schematic
circuits.description: A controller selects which of two system lines reaches its own signal line. One controller output drives IN, held low by a resistor to ground so COM rests on NC until the output drives it high; a second controller line connects to COM. NO and NC go out to the system. V+ is decoupled to ground at the pin.

parts.note: V+ bypass, as close to the pin as possible
size set by the GPIO drive, power budget and switching rate

notes: V+ is 5 V in this circuit; the design example uses V+ = 1.8 V, and any supply from 1.65 V to 5.5 V applies.
With an open-drain GPIO a pull-up takes the place of R1.

circuits.title: ON-state resistance (ron)
circuits.description: A DC source is switched onto NC or NO, the control voltage closes that channel, and a current source draws ICOM out of COM to ground; ron is the voltage across the switch divided by ICOM.

parts.note: applies V1 to NC or NO

notes: ron = (VCOM - VNO or VNC) / ICOM with VI = VIH or VIL.

circuits.title: OFF-state leakage current
circuits.description: A DC source on NC or NO and a second on COM, with the channel between them open; the current into each terminal is the OFF leakage. With V+ = 0 the same setup gives the power-off leakages.

parts.note: applies V1 to NC or NO

notes: Channel OFF, VI = VIH or VIL.

circuits.title: ON-state leakage current
circuits.description: A DC source on NC or NO with the channel closed and COM left open; the current flowing in is the ON leakage.

parts.note: applies V1 to NC or NO

notes: Channel ON, VI = VIH or VIL.

circuits.title: Capacitance (CI, CCOM(ON), CNC(OFF), CNO(OFF), CNC(ON), CNO(ON))
circuits.description: A capacitance meter, biased at VBIAS, is switched onto one terminal at a time (NC, NO, COM or IN) with the channel ON or OFF, and reads that terminal's capacitance.

parts.note: connects the meter to the terminal under test

notes: Capacitance is measured at NC, NO, COM and IN, with the channel ON and OFF.

circuits.title: Turnon (tON) and turnoff time (tOFF)
circuits.description: COM is held at V+ and each of NC and NO drives 50 Ω in parallel with 35 pF to ground. A logic pulse on IN switches the channels; tON and tOFF run from the 50% point of the control edge to 90% of the output swing.
notes: Logic pulses come from a generator with PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr and tf < 5 ns; CL counts probe and jig capacitance.
Either channel, NC or NO, may be the one timed.

circuits.title: Make-before-break time (tMBB)
circuits.description: COM is held at V+ and NC and NO each drive 50 Ω in parallel with 35 pF to ground. When IN changes state the closing channel's output passes 0.8 × VOUT before the opening channel's output falls through 0.8 × VOUT; the time between the two crossings is tMBB.
notes: Logic pulses come from a generator with PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr and tf < 5 ns; CL counts probe and jig capacitance.

circuits.title: Bandwidth (BW)
circuits.description: A network analyzer drives NC through its 50 Ω source with the NC channel closed, and reads COM across its 50 Ω input; BW is where the gain is 3 dB below its DC value. NO is left open.
notes: Channel ON: NC to COM.
Network analyzer source power 0 dBm (632 mV peak to peak into 50 Ω), DC bias 350 mV; VI = V+ or GND.

circuits.title: OFF isolation (OISO)
circuits.description: The analyzer drives NC, terminated in 50 Ω to ground, with the NC channel open, and reads what reaches COM across its 50 Ω input. NO is left open.
notes: Channel OFF: NC to COM.
Network analyzer source power 0 dBm (632 mV peak to peak into 50 Ω), DC bias 350 mV; VI = V+ or GND.

circuits.title: Crosstalk (XTALK)
circuits.description: The analyzer drives NC through the closed NC channel into 50 Ω at COM, and reads what couples onto the open NO terminal across its 50 Ω input.
notes: Channel ON: NC to COM; channel OFF: NO to COM.
Network analyzer source power 0 dBm (632 mV peak to peak into 50 Ω), DC bias 350 mV; VI = V+ or GND.

circuits.title: Charge injection (QC)
circuits.description: A source VGEN behind RGEN feeds NC or NO; COM is loaded by CL alone. IN is pulsed off, on and off, and the step ΔVCOM left on CL, multiplied by CL, is the injected charge.
notes: Logic pulses come from a generator with PRR ≤ 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω, tr and tf < 5 ns; CL counts probe and jig capacitance.
The source may feed either NC or NO; the other is left open.

where.CL: load capacitance on COM, 1 nF in test
where.ΔVCOM: step in COM voltage when IN switches

operation.text: IN low closes COM to NC; IN high closes COM to NO. The paths conduct in both directions. Switching is make-before-break: the new path closes before the old one opens, so for a brief interval NC and NO are joined to each other through COM.

Signals from 0 V to V+ pass with low distortion; ON resistance is lowest and flattest at the higher supplies (about 0.5 Ω to 0.9 Ω over the range at 5 V) and peaks near mid-range at 1.8 V, around 3.3 Ω.
With V+ = 0 the switch terminals stay isolated; the power-off leakage at NC, NO and COM is at most ±1 µA at 25 °C.

IN tolerates 5.5 V at every supply voltage. It must always be driven high or low: a floating input or one held near threshold partly turns on its input transistors, raising supply current and leaving the selected path undefined. Unused NC, NO or COM terminals may float or be grounded.

In the system schematic a resistor pulls IN to ground, so COM sits on NC until the controller drives IN high. Its value depends on how much current the GPIO can source, the power that may be spent in it and how often IN switches. A GPIO with an open-drain output needs a pull-up in its place.
Any supply within 1.65 V to 5.5 V may be used. Fit a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor at V+, as close to the pin as possible; 0.1 µF and 1 µF may be paralleled to cover a wider band of noise.
A square 90° trace corner widens the track to about 1.414 times its width at the bend and causes a reflection. Two 45° bends are better; a rounded corner that keeps the width constant is best.
